updates.coverageDescription: Applies to residential rental buildings with first certificate of occupancy before February 1, 1995. The rent increase limit of 3% or 80% CPI (whichever is less) applies to these properties; buildings constructed after February 1, 1995 are exempt.
updates.coverageQuote: The rent cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995

updates.coverageDescription: Applies to residential rental buildings with first certificate of occupancy before February 1, 1995. Residential rent increases are limited annually to the lower of 3% or 80% of CPI change. If CPI is negative, no increase is permitted. Buildings constructed after February 1, 1995 are exempt.
updates.coverageQuote: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index

updates.coverageDescription: Applies to residential rental buildings not produced in the last 15 years (as of the ordinance adoption in 2021). For no-fault terminations (owner occupancy, removal from rental market, or demolition/substantial remodel), landlord must provide 3 months relocation assistance or waive 3 months rent. Buildings produced within the last 15 years are exempt.
updates.coverageQuote: housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing

updates.coverageDescription: Applies to residential rental buildings not produced in the last 15 years (as of ordinance adoption in 2021). A landlord must have a valid reason to evict, including non-payment of rent, breach of lease, or owner occupancy intent. Buildings produced within the last 15 years are exempt.
updates.coverageQuote: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause
